scenes.heading: Angle properties review
scenes.say: Roof trusses, road crossings and floor tiles all depend on a few angle rules. In this video you will pull all of them together, so you can solve multi-step angle problems and give a reason for every step.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: All the slices of a pizza make the whole pizza
scenes.science: Angles at a point make 360°; half the pizza is a straight line, 180°
scenes.breaks: Pizza explains points and lines, but parallel-line rules need the F, Z and C shapes instead.
scenes.say: Think of a pizza cut from the centre. All the slices make the whole pizza, just as angles around a point make three hundred and sixty degrees. Half the pizza is a straight line: one hundred and eighty degrees. But pizza says nothing about parallel lines, so for those you need the F, Z and C shapes.
scenes.caption: All the slices make the whole pizza, just as angles at a point make 360°. Half the pizza is a straight line: 180°. For parallel lines you need the F, Z and C shapes.

scenes.heading: F, Z and C with parallel lines
scenes.say: First the two parallel lines, then the transversal, then the angles. Seventy degrees at the top. The matching angle at the bottom, a, is also seventy: corresponding angles. b sits on a straight line with a, so it is one hundred and ten, and c plus b make a C shape: co-interior angles add to one hundred and eighty.
scenes.caption: Seventy degrees at the top. a is also 70°: corresponding angles. b is on a straight line with a, so b = 110°, and c + b make a C shape: co-interior angles add to 180°.

scenes.heading: The exterior angle of a triangle
scenes.say: Now a triangle with angles of fifty and sixty degrees. Extend one side, and the exterior angle at B is fifty plus sixty, which is one hundred and ten degrees. It always equals the two inside angles that are not next to it.
scenes.caption: A triangle with angles of 50° and 60°. Extend one side: the exterior angle at B is 50° + 60° = 110°.

scenes.heading: Polygon angle sum
scenes.say: For any polygon, the interior angles add to n minus two, times one hundred and eighty degrees, because the polygon splits into n minus two triangles. The exterior angles always add to three hundred and sixty.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: A pentagon has angles 100°, 110°, 95°, 120° and x. Find x.
scenes.say: A pentagon has angles of one hundred, one hundred and ten, ninety-five, one hundred and twenty and x. The angle sum is three times one eighty, which is five hundred and forty. The known angles add to four hundred and twenty-five, so x is one hundred and fifteen degrees.
scenes.caption: The angle sum is 3 × 180° = 540°. The known angles add to 425°, so x = 115°.

points: F and Z angles are equal; C angles add to 180°
Exterior angle = sum of the far two
scenes.say: Quick recap. Straight line one eighty, point three sixty. F and Z angles are equal, C angles add to one eighty. An exterior angle equals the two far inside angles. A polygon adds to n minus two times one eighty. And give a reason for every step. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: Straight line 180°, point 360°. F and Z angles are equal, C angles add to 180°. An exterior angle equals the two far inside angles. A polygon adds to (n − 2) × 180°. Give a reason for every step. Now try the practice questions!
